newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money rates slump, gilts volume rises.
newsitem.headline: India call money rates slump, gilts volume rises.

text.p: Indian call money slumped to 5.00-5.25 percent at close against the day's opening levels of 6.50-7.50 percent, dealers said.
"The market saw some fluctuation after opening at 7.25, dropping to today's low of 4.5 percent before closing at 5.25 percent," a dealer said. "Some late demand pushed up rates from the day's low."
Volumes in the securities market picked up on lower call rates, dealers said.
Trades on the National Stock Exchange improved to 880 million rupees on Wednesday against the previous day's 610 million rupees.
The 13.55 percent 2001 stock was traded at 100.25 rupees and 100.26 rupees, dealers said.

Yield on treasury bills maturing in December 1997 rose to 10.35 percent from the previous day's 10.25 percent, while the yield on treasury bills maturing in January 1997 fell by 30 basis points to 8.25 percent, dealers said.
State Bank of India certificates of deposits maturing in January 1997 was traded at 10.50 percent, a dealer said.
He said the market also witnessed some low volume trades in commercial papers.
